Article Title: Delhi protest crackdown: 20 FIRs registered, assault on cops among charges
Article Text:
The protest, which called for Kumar's resignation, was met with a massive security deployment and widespread detentions across the national capital

Supreme Court steps in over restrictions

CJP alleges 'open Emergency'

NEW DELHI: Delhi Police has registered 20 FIRs in connection with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, officials told news agency PTI on Sunday.The cases include charges of assaulting police personnel and obstructing public servants from discharging their duties. One FIR registered at Kamla Market police station relates to the alleged assault on students and manhandling of women during the protest. Four men claiming links to the right-wing Hindu Raksha Dal have been arrested in the case, officials said.The protest, which called for Kumar's resignation, was met with a massive security deployment and widespread detentions across the national capital on Saturday. More than 7,000 people, including opposition leaders and activists, were detained as police erected barricades and deployed thousands of personnel to prevent demonstrators from reaching Jantar Mantar. Several incidents of stone-throwing were reported, leaving more than 15 police personnel injured, including Deputy Commissioner of Police (South) Anant Mittal.Amid the fallout, the Supreme Court on Sunday directed authorities to ensure that people gathering peacefully are not illegally detained and that Delhi Metro services operate normally, subject to law and order conditions.The bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also directed that internet services remain undisturbed and that lawyers and journalists not be obstructed from performing their professional duties.The court issued a notice to the Centre while hearing a plea seeking contempt proceedings over alleged violations of its directions concerning restrictions on metro and train services during the protest. It also ordered authorities to remove a notice board outside the Supreme Court premises announcing the imposition of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which restricts assemblies of five or more people.Meanwhile, CJP activists Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka accused the administration of imposing excessive restrictions to suppress what they described as a youth-led movement."The situation across the country right now mirrors an open Emergency. Such repressive conditions have not been witnessed since the dictatorial regime of 1975," Das said, alleging that Delhi had been turned into a "cantonment".He also criticised the closure of metro stations, suspension of train services and shutdown of markets, claiming the restrictions were inconveniencing ordinary citizens and turning public sentiment against the protest.Ranka separately condemned the police's handling of activist Abhijeet Dipke, alleging that personnel showed insensitivity while informing him of his grandmother's death.
Article Summary: Delhi Police has registered 20 FIRs in connection with the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP)-led protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The cases include charges of assaulting police personnel and obstructing public servants from discharging their duties. Four men claiming links to the right- wing Hindu Raksha Dal have been arrested in the case.

Article Title: Watch: CPM MP John Brittas argues with Delhi Police as they attempt to detain him
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: CPM Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas on Sunday got into a heated argument with Delhi Police personnel as they attempted to detain him amid a political row over the detention of Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) chief Abhijeet Dipke and other party leaders.Brittas, along with CPM MP A A Rahim, had criticised the police action against Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das, who were reportedly detained aboard their flight from Mumbai after it landed at Indira Gandhi International Airport on Saturday.Speaking to reporters in Delhi, Brittas said the CJP leaders had been treated worse than hijackers or people accused of major financial scams.“The central government is doing all this because they are scared. The police could have arrested them once they come out of the airport. They could not have escaped from inside the airport. There was no need to detain them from inside the plane,” he said.Brittas also condemned the action against journalists, alleging that several were detained or prevented from reporting on the protests, PTI reported.He accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah of taking such measures to protect Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Rahim alleged that several CJP activists and protesters who resisted restrictions on the demonstration at Jantar Mantar or objected to the removal of their phones were “brutally tortured”.Dipke, Ranka and Das were released on Sunday after being produced before the Special Executive Magistrate (SEM) Court at Delhi Cantonment Police Station.Delhi Police said the three were preventively arrested under Sections 126 and 170 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) on October 10 and produced before the court on October 11.The police said the three were released after furnishing a surety bond of Rs 50,000, with a condition to maintain peace and good behaviour for one year.CJP legal affairs head Ratna Singh also confirmed their release, saying it was subject to an undertaking to maintain public order. “Condition - no breach of peace for one year,” she posted on X.Before his release, Dipke had alleged in a video posted on Instagram that Delhi Police personnel entered his flight to detain him and his associates after they landed in Delhi.“So, you can see that Delhi Police is entering the plane to arrest us. They are all entering the plane. We just landed. All the Delhi Police officers are standing in the aisle. They are trying to arrest us from inside the plane. The entire Delhi Police is getting on the plane. This is the fear of Narendra Modi...Not even Indira Gandhi did this during the Emergency. All we wanted to do is a peaceful protest, and they are picking us up from the flight like we are criminals,” Dipke said.The detention of the CJP leaders came amid a major security clampdown in Delhi on Saturday. Delhi Police detained protesters, activists and political leaders at multiple locations, including along routes leading to Jantar Mantar, where the CJP had planned to hold a demonstration.The party and opposition groups have been demanding Kumar’s resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Delhi Police had denied permission for the gathering, and many protesters were detained before they could reach the proposed venue.More than 7,000 protesters were detained at multiple locations, according to the details provided. Several opposition leaders, including former chief ministers Arvind Kejriwal, Mamata Banerjee, Pinarayi Vijayan and Manik Sarkar, were also detained while attempting to join the protest.
Article Summary: CPM Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas got into a heated argument with Delhi Police personnel as they attempted to detain him. Brittas, along with CPM MP A A Rahim, had criticised the police action against Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das. They were reportedly detained aboard their flight from Mumbai after it landed at Indira Gandhi International Airport.

Article Title: India condemns 'dastardly' attacks on Saudi Arabia's Riyadh airport that killed 12
Article Text:
India condemns attacks on Khalid International Airport in Riyadh

NEW DELHI: India on Sunday strongly condemned repeated attacks on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 12 people and injured more than 300.“We strongly condemn the repeated attacks on Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport over the past few days, including the dastardly attack on October 10, which have led to loss of lives, injuries and damage to property,” the ministry of external affairs (MEA) said.“We express our condolences to the families of the deceased and wish speedy recovery to the injured persons. The repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are completely unacceptable and must cease immediately,” it added.India also expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia, saying it stood with the country and its people in defending their sovereignty and hoped peace and normalcy would return to the region soon.Meanwhile, the US also condemned the attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airport.Asked whether Washington had decided to join the strikes against the Houthis in Saudi Arabia, US President Donald Trump said, “We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack. We will make a decision. We move very quickly.”He added, “Look, the Saudis are good fighters. But I think the attack was a terrible thing.”King Khalid International Airport has faced multiple attacks over the past week, following the launch of a major military offensive by a Saudi-led coalition against Iran-backed Houthi rebels in neighbouring Yemen.Earlier attacks on King Khalid International Airport and Abha International Airport on October 6 and 7 reportedly killed three people and injured 36, according to the General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA).Following the latest attack, airport operations were temporarily suspended and travellers were evacuated. Dozens of ambulances were seen rushing to the site.The airport also issued an alert asking passengers to check their flight status with airlines before leaving for the airport.According to flight-tracking platform Flightradar24, flights heading to Riyadh were being diverted to other destinations nearly four hours after the last flight landed at 2.05 pm local time. FlightAware reported that at least 225 flights at King Khalid International Airport had been cancelled in the preceding 24 hours.
Article Summary: India condemns repeated attacks on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh that killed 12 people and injured more than 300. India also expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia, saying it stood with the country and its people in defending their sovereignty.

NEW DELHI: Rashtriya Janata Dal ( RJD ) MP Manoj Jha has approached the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi Police ’s handling of protests held in the national capital on October 10 against chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission.The plea alleges disproportionate use of force, illegal detentions and house arrests of protesters, including student leaders, advocates, politicians and civilians.It also raises allegations of sexual harassment of women protesters and claims that the police failed to act against individuals who allegedly assaulted demonstrators, according to Live Law report.Jha has claimed that more than 6,000 people, including former chief ministers, MPs, senior advocates, lawyers, students and civilians unconnected with the protests, were detained by the authorities.The petition states that 250 trains were reportedly cancelled ahead of the demonstrations and 45 Metro stations in Delhi were closed on October 10. NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Sunday directed authorities to ensure that people gathering peacefully are not illegally detained and that metro and railway services function normally. The court's directive came a day after Centre's crackdown on CJP's proposed protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.The court issued notice to the Centre on a plea seeking contempt proceedings against authorities for allegedly violating its earlier directions on transport restrictions during the protest.“In view of the urgent applications alleging violation of our earlier order dt. October 9, 2026, and also alleging illegal detention of large number of individuals at Delhi on October 10, 2026 this court had assembled for an urgent hearing,” a bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said during a special sitting.“Senior counsels submitted there was a flagrant violation of the directions -- metro railway was not functioning, New Delhi and Nizamuddin railway stations remained closed, no traffic advisories were issued and a large number of persons were subjected to undue harassment and illegal detention even beyond the area which was covered by the prohibitory order under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023,” the bench said.The Supreme Court asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to ensure that the Delhi Metro operated according to its normal schedule and that internet services were not disrupted, subject to law and order conditions. It also directed that lawyers, journalists and others should not be impeded from discharging their professional duties.Mehta, appearing for the Centre, defended the authorities’ action and submitted that entry and exit had been restricted at only 45 of the 303 stations across the Delhi Metro network on October 10.The court was also hearing a habeas corpus petition filed by senior advocate Menaka Guruswamy concerning the detention of political leaders. It said it would grant a hearing to all lawyers involved in the matter.The contempt petition, filed by advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, names Union home secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro Rail Corporation chairperson D Thara as respondents.The plea refers to the Supreme Court’s October 9 order, passed while hearing a separate petition challenging the closure of 57 metro stations and the cancellation of trains to Delhi in view of the proposed protest. The latest applications alleged that the restrictions and detentions on October 10 violated the court’s directions.The court’s intervention followed the CJP’s call for a mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar, alongside student organisations, demanding action against CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission.The government thwarted the planned demonstration through an extensive security crackdown across the national capital. More than 7,000 protesters were detained, including CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, several opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.

The court's directive came a day after Centre's crackdown on CJP's proposed protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. More than 7,000 protesters were detained, including CJP leader Abhijit Dipke.

Article Title: Restrained, detained, contained: Clampdown foils stir, thousands confined to home, nabbed on way
Article Text:
Security arrangements may not see let-up today

NEW DELHI: Unprecedented security arrangements from central Delhi to the borders, phalanxes of 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel and a virtual choke on metro services and trains foiled Cockroach Janta Party's march to Jantar Mantar on Saturday. The city, however, remained on edge, with young protesters being detained on their way to the protest site and bundled into buses and vans, kicking and screaming, through the day.With CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das detained at the airport, the outfit's national organisation in-charge, Ajinkya Shinde, was named to lead the protests. The computer science grad, a former AAP worker, said protests would continue till Gyanesh Kumar resigned as CEC.With top CJP functionaries being kept away from Jantar Mantar, small groups dodged security personnel and staged flash protests at Safdarjung flyover, Dilli Haat and Gurdwara Bangla Sahib complex, among other places.The impromptu gathering near Safdarjung flyover by AISA national president Neha Bora, lawyer Prashant Bhushan, political commentator Yogendra Yadav, and several others caught police off-guard momentarily around 1pm.The protesters were eventually detained.It was obvious since Thursday that the call by CJP, supported by some political outfits, for a protest against the CEC and SIR at Jantar Mantar at 10am on Saturday would be met with stiff resistance. New Delhi was divided into 20 zones, with 1-2 companies of CAPF and Delhi Police deployed at every nook and corner. BSF was also present at the city's borders.Water cannons and tear-gas vehicles were kept ready. Multiple layers of barricades were erected and police personnel closely questioned people heading towards the New Delhi area, particularly in the direction of Jantar Mantar. Police said there were only some isolated incidents of minor confrontations. While three or four personnel, including women, were injured in incidents of stone-pelting and other skirmishes, a DCP fractured his hand, they said.Police claimed they had detained 2,500 people in the city — 600-700 people on stretches leading to Jantar Mantar, and others from different parts of Delhi, including the borders. The police figures were, however, hotly contested, with sources saying around 7,000 people were detained, counting those who were not allowed to leave their homes and were put under preventive detention.CJP’s Ajinkya Shinde, who will lead the protests now, alleged more than 15,000 people, including students, civil society members and political functionaries, had been illegally detained across the country. An undeclared emergency had been imposed in Delhi, he said.Police said apart from the fact that permission had not been given for the protest, prohibitory orders under Section 163 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) were in force, making the proposed gathering illegal.Four former chief ministers — Aam Aadmi Party convener Arvind Kejriwal, Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee, Kerala’s Pinarayi Vijayan, and Manik Sarkar of Tripura — were detained. CPM veteran Brinda Karat, Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas, and TMC functionaries Derek O’Brien and Dola Sen were also detained.Detained protesters were taken in buses to Chhatrasal Stadium, Rajiv Gandhi Stadium, Yamuna Sports Complex and Surajmal Stadium, all designated earlier for this purpose. Around 600 buses, including some from Third Battalion used to transport prisoners, were used to ferry those detained.Around 9pm, police claimed they had released everyone, but refused to respond when asked about Dipke, Ranka and Das. Multiple cases will be registered in connection with violation of prohibitory orders and assault, besides other sections, police said.With CJP sources saying they will continue their protests and Congress and other INDIA bloc parties planning a march in the city Monday, the security paraphernalia is likely to remain in place for the next few days.
Article Summary: CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das detained at the airport. Ajinkya Shinde, CJP's national organisation in-charge, named to lead the protests. Police claim they had detained 2,500 people in the city.

Article Title: Anxiety treatable, but 83% of affected did not get help
Article Text:
The invisible burden

When the body's alarm won't switch off

Life in the slow lane

It's treatable

Whenever Thane businessman Shekhar travels to south Mumbai for a meeting, he sets off over three hours early. This is because he plans his route carefully to ensure he is never more than five minutes from a hospital in case he "suffers a heart attack while driving".Karthik (32), an IIM graduate with a high-powered marketing job, dreads routine meetings. "There is this heaviness in my stomach and my legs seem leaden. It's a paralysing fear that stays until the meeting is over," he says.Shekhar and Karthik (names changed) have anxiety disorders, a group of conditions that can turn ordinary journeys, workplace interactions and social situations into emotional ordeals.National Mental Health Survey, conducted by National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS) across 12 states between 2014 and 2016, found that 2.57% of adults had an anxiety disorder at the time of assessment.Around 83% of those affected were not receiving treatment, while nearly 60% experienced disability of varying severity, according to the study published in the Indian Journal of Psychiatry in 2022."Anxiety disorders are frequently under-recognised and inadequately treated. Stigma surrounding mental illness and a lack of awareness contribute to the problem," said psychiatrist Dr Kedar Tilwe of Fortis Hospital, Mulund.Child psychiatrist Dr Kersi Chavda said anxiety can take many forms, from social anxiety and academic stress to persistent, intrusive thoughts.In children, it may manifest as school refusal. Among adolescents facing examinations, anxiety can also present as headaches, body aches or backaches.Social anxiety is another concern, said Dr Chavda. The pressure to appear perfect, amplified by curated virtual lives on social media, can intensify the fear of being judged or found wanting.Everyday anxiety is a normal response to uncertainty or danger. An anxiety disorder involves persistent or disproportionate fear that interferes with daily life.A senior psychologist from a civic hospital linked anxiety to the body's built-in alarm system. The alarm is meant to respond to a threat, but sometimes it reacts to a gust of wind as though an intruder were approaching.Psychiatrist Dr Harish Shetty said, "Crowded trains, inadequate sleep, workplace demands, educational pressures, financial worries and concerns about personal safety can keep people in a state of heightened stress."Weakening support systems and reduced emotional connectedness may also be contributing, said Dr Shetty.In adults, panic disorder can be accompanied by agoraphobia - fear of situations where escape might be difficult or help unavailable if a panic attack occurs."Patients may avoid bri-dges, crowded trains, flights or traffic jams. Some will not travel without their spouses or may turn down promotions or jobs that require them to venture beyond familiar surroundi-ngs," said Dr Tilwe. As a result, he added, it's a life lived in second gear: not ready to take up new challenges as one prefers to stick to known schedules.Anxiety disorders are treatable, but a trained physician is needed to recognise the problem. Treatment depends on the type and severity of the disorder and may involve psychotherapy, medication or both. "A person with a severe anxiety disorder may need counselling along with medication for up to six months to be able to cope," said Dr Tilwe.Dr Shetty recommends attention to sleep, time management, breathing exercises and meditation. Doctors said reducing excessive caffeine and smoking would help some people manage symptoms.
Article Summary: Anxiety disorders are treatable, but a trained physician is needed to recognise the problem. Treatment depends on the type and severity of the disorder and may involve psychotherapy, medication or both. The pressure to appear perfect, amplified by curated virtual lives on social media, can intensify the fear of being judged or found wanting.

NEW DELHI: National Investigation Agency has filed an FIR under the Anti-Hijacking Act and UAPA to probe the failed hijacking of a flydubai aircraft. On Sept 30, the flight's Omani co-pilot, Hamam al-Hammami, had stabbed Indian captain Smit Machchhar inside the cockpit.The move follows a central govt directive to probe the possible implications of the attack, thwart future bids and detect any cells active in connection with the incident."The gravity of the offence, its grave national and international ramifications and the need to unearth the larger conspiracy require a thorough probe by the NIA," the agency said in the FIR, describing the incident as an apparent attempt to hijack or crash flydubai Flight 1073.The move comes amid al-Qaida in Indian Subcontinent (AQIS) endorsing the incident in the latest issue of its magazine Nawa-e-Gazwa-e-Hind. AQIS framed the co-pilot's actions as a response to Hamas commander Muhammad Deif's call to reclaim Al-Aqsa Mosque and linked them to Bin Laden's rhetoric.Last week, al-Bayan, another publication linked to the terror outfit, called for a "ten times greater attack than 9/11" and the end of the "American empire". Neither publication, however, claimed responsibility for the attack.AQIS said the attempt had created psychological fear and economic strain for the United States, Israel and their allies despite falling short of its primary goal.
Article Summary: National Investigation Agency has filed an FIR under the Anti-Hijacking Act and UAPA to probe the failed hijacking of a flydubai aircraft. On Sept 30, the flight's Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami had stabbed Indian captain Smit Machchhar inside the cockpit.

Welcome to the New Delhi, modelled on the New Jammu and Kashmir,” he posted on X.PDP president Mehbooba Mufti accused the BJP of presenting restrictions on protests as public consent, drawing parallels with the lockdown in Kashmir in 2019.“This is how enforced silence is passed off as consent,” she said.Senior advocate and Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal questioned the legality of detaining people travelling to Delhi to join the demonstration.“If a person or a community wants to protest peacefully, then who is in danger? Bora had led a march from Jor Bagh towards Dilli Haat-INA.CJP named Ajinkya Shinde to lead the protest in a pre-recorded video. Following the announcement, Ajinkya urged protesters to turn any location where police stopped them into their “Jantar Mantar”.Congress MP Shashi Tharoor described the situation as an “undeclared Emer-GenZ”. He criticised the heavy security deployment, train cancellations, metro closures and restrictions on movement.Former Delhi CM Arvind Kejriwal, former Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee were detained while heading to join the protest. Mamata said they had been taken around in a prisoner van for two hours. She announced a sit-in at Dwarka North police station and said she would join the INDIA march on Monday.Congress leaders Mallikarjun Kharge and Priyanka Gandhi criticised the crackdown ahead of the planned protest. Kharge accused the Modi government of suppressing dissent, saying it had turned the “mother of democracy” into a "muzzled democracy”. Meanwhile, Priyanka alleged that the government had curtailed constitutional rights.Police officials reported stones being pelted at a bus carrying detained protesters in Jhandewalan. Two police personnel, including a Pink Force member, were reported injured. Another officer was injured in alleged stone-pelting near Baba Kharak Singh Marg in Connaught Place, where police said a scuffle broke out as they tried to disperse protesters.By late afternoon, the reported detention count had risen from at least 600 in the morning to around 1,000 by afternoon.BJP spokesperson Sambit Patra accused Rahul Gandhi of attempting to drag the President into a street protest. The party defended the police action, describing it as a victory for democracy over “mob rule”. Nabin had earlier accused the protesters of trying to destabilise the country.Chief Justice of India Surya Kant communicated to authorities that lawyers detained while peacefully protesting outside the Supreme Court should be released. The intervention followed an urgent letter from the Supreme Court Bar Association, which said several advocates had been taken to the Yamuna Sports Complex.CPM general secretary MA Baby filed a petition in the Supreme Court challenging restrictions imposed ahead of the protest, including curbs on metro services and mobile internet connectivity. TMC spokesperson Saket Gokhale also wrote to the Delhi high court’s acting chief justice, seeking suo motu intervention over the transport restrictions.Rahul Gandhi targeted PM Modi, Amit Shah, RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat, CEC Gyanesh Kumar and national security adviser Ajit Doval. He accused them of attacking the Constitution and vowed to continue the fight to defend democratic rights. Mamata Banerjee said she would remain in Delhi and join the INDIA march on Monday, in protest against the treatment of young people and other protesters.Meanwhile, an open letter signed by 124 former IAS and IFS officers strongly defended the Election Commission and the SIR process, adding to the debate over the electoral-roll revision.CJP in a press conference announced to march to Jantar Mantar again on Sunday.It said they will "not back down until demands are met" after mass detentions and alleged the Modi government feared that a united opposition could threaten its hold on power.
Article Summary: Delhi Police detained more than 7,000 people across the national capital. Those detained included CJP leaders, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) national convenor Arvind Kejriwal, former Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee. Police also placed several Congress workers and members of other political parties under house arrest ahead of the demonstration.

Article Title: ‘Rigged when you lose?’ 124 former bureaucrats defend EC & SIR, challenge vote-rigging claims
Article Text:
Former civil servants, including ex-Foreign Secretary Kanwal Sibal, former Ambassadors, and retired IAS officers, issued a joint open letter defending India's electoral integrity.

NEW DELHI: A group of 124 former IAS, IFS and allied services officers has issued an open letter to citizens defending the Election Commission (EC) and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, arguing that allegations of vote rigging must be backed by credible evidence.Citing safeguards in the electoral process, past election results and data from Bihar’s 2025 Assembly polls, the signatories have challenged claims questioning the credibility of the EC and the need for SIR.The officers said India's electoral system had evolved significantly from an era marked by booth capturing, ballot-box stuffing and electoral violence. They cited multiple safeguards in the present system, including polling agents, electronic voting machine (EVM) sealing, strong-room security and voter-verified paper audit trail (VVPAT) verification.Referring to the 2025 Bihar Assembly elections, the signatories said the polls recorded no re-polling and the highest voter turnout since 1951."A system cannot be honest when you win and rigged when you lose," the letter said, pointing out that the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), which leads the government at the Centre, had lost several state elections under the same EC and also lost its parliamentary majority in 2024.The signatories include former foreign secretary Kanwal Sibal and former IAS officers R D Kapur, Samirendra Chatterjee, Gopal Krishna, Vivek Bhardwaj and Navneet Sehgal.Defending the EC's independence, the officers highlighted its multi-member structure and institutional safeguards. They also drew a distinction between questioning the electoral process and substantiating allegations against it."Questioning is every citizen's right. Proving is the accuser's duty," the letter said.On SIR, the officers argued that the exercise was necessary to maintain accurate electoral rolls. Citing figures from Bihar, they referred to around 22 lakh deceased voters and seven lakh duplicate entries identified during the revision, alongside the addition of approximately 21.5 lakh new voters."An uncleaned roll does not protect the voter. It protects the fraudster," the letter said.The officers also pointed to safeguards available during SIR, including notices, hearings, appeals and the participation of political parties' booth-level agents. They said the Supreme Court had scrutinised the exercise, prescribed additional safeguards and upheld the EC's authority to undertake it.Concluding their argument, the signatories urged critics to examine allegations against the electoral system consistently, irrespective of election outcomes."If the system you call rigged is the same one that handed you your victories, ask yourself whether it is the system you doubt, or only the result," the letter said.
Article Summary: 124 former IAS, IFS and allied services officers have issued an open letter to citizens defending the Election Commission (EC) They argue that allegations of vote rigging must be backed by credible evidence. The officers said India's electoral system had evolved significantly from an era marked by booth capturing, ballot-box stuffing and electoral violence.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu minister Aadhav Arjuna launched a sharp attack on the DMK, claiming that the party had underestimated his side and was now in a weak position in the Maduranthakam constituency.Arjuna said the DMK had earlier claimed it would win 200 constituencies but was now sitting in the opposition benches.“The DMK, which said that it would win 200 constituencies, is sitting in the Opposition benches. They took us lightly. They said, ‘These people only know how to blow whistles.’ That very whistle came to us as our symbol, and we have blown them away completely with that whistle,” he said.Arjuna further claimed that the DMK was in a “pathetic position” in the constituency and questioned whether the party would even be able to retain its election deposit.“In this constituency, the DMK is in a pathetic position. Will the DMK even get its deposit back?” he said.He also targeted Tamil Nadu leader of opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin , alleging that his remarks were damaging the DMK.“Everything that comes out of the mouth of Udhayanidhi is only obscenity. No one else needs to come to destroy the DMK; MK Stalin’s son is enough. Udhayanidhi Stalin has come to destroy the DMK,” Arjuna said.Bypolls to the Maduranthakam Assembly constituency in Chengelpet district, adjoining Chennai, and the Dharapuram constituency in Tiruppur district of western Tamil Nadu will be held on October 6.The bypolls were necessitated after AIADMK legislators Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabama resigned from their posts and joined the ruling TVK. The party has fielded both of them from the same constituencies they represented after being elected in the April Assembly election.This is the first time the TVK government is facing Assembly bypolls since it assumed office in May 2026.The Left parties, which extend outside support to the TVK government and help it retain its majority, have not joined the ruling party-led alliance. Instead, they are contesting the bypolls as a separate front.Candidates of the main opposition DMK, the AIADMK and the Tamil nationalist Naam Tamilar Katchi (NTK) are also in the fray.The Vanniyar-dominated PMK, which has considerable influence in several northern parts of the state, has not extended support to any party.A key opposition campaign plank is that the bypolls were not a natural outcome but were forced on voters after the TVK “lured AIADMK MLAs” to strengthen its numbers in the Assembly.AIADMK chief Edappadi K Palaniswami has already begun campaigning, seeking “justice” over what he has described as the betrayal.
